boscombe-surf-reef.datum: metres ODN (Ordnance Datum Newlyn) of the CCO profiles; the 3D model takes ODN = MSL within +-0.1 m (A4, METHODS_3D 3.2), so 0 m ODN ~ MSL contour
boscombe-surf-reef.data_source: Channel Coastal Observatory (CCO) beach-profile surveys, lines 5f00424-5f00429 (+ "A" lines 424A-428A from 2010), 316 files 07_scale/shapes/boscombe-surf-reef/src/cco_profiles/<line>_<date>.txt, fetched by 3d/scripts/cco_fetch.py (see 3d/SOURCES_3D.md S13); points (E,N,z_ODN,chainage) converted to the canonical reef frame with 3d/scripts/canon.py (OSGB36 -> canonical, +-5 m). Profiles run from the sea wall (y about -64 m) to z about -1 m ODN (y about +21 m); the reef lies at y = 181-276 m, i.e. >= 160 m seaward of the end of every profile.

Ls_over_X.note: DERIVED B/S (B = Ls alongshore extent, S = X shoreline-to-reef distance). Rules (Black & Andrews 2001 via Blacka et al. 2013): no change if B/S < ~0.1, salient if < 2, tombolo if > 0.6; Blacka et al. note the method over-predicts salient size for submerged reefs (Narrowneck, Mount Maunganui). Illustrative amplitude = 0.125 x D_tot with D_tot = 1-3 B (ASSUMPTION; D_tot is not given in the secondary source) -> an order of magnitude only. shoreline = mean post-construction 0 m ODN contour of the lee lines (y = -4.0 m)

B_common_mode_volume_jumps.definition: year-to-year rise of the beach volume above 0 m ODN (between y=-55 m and the 0 m contour) with a median over the 6 main lines > 20 m3 per m. DERIVED indicator only: the dates and volumes of Poole Bay recharge / recycling are NOT in the repo (ASSUMPTION that such jumps are beach management, not natural; the CCO and BCP Council beach-management records must be checked).

C_common_mode_removed_BACI.definition: For each date on which all six main lines were surveyed, the line value minus the mean of the six lines (removes common-mode beach-management and seasonal signal). change_rel = post mean minus pre mean per line. lee_anomaly = mean change_rel of the lee lines (5f00426, 5f00427) minus the straight-line trend fitted to the control lines (5f00424, 5f00425, 5f00428, 5f00429) at the lee-line positions; POSITIVE = lee shoreline advanced (or volume rose) relative to the controls after the reef. 95 % CI by bootstrap over survey dates (4000 resamples; pre n=5 dates, post n=17 dates).

D_post_only_alongshore_pattern_11_lines.definition: Post-construction annual surveys on which all 11 lines (6 main + 5 "A") exist; position minus the 11-line mean; anomaly of the lee lines against the straight line through the control lines (|x - xc| >= 1.5 L) per date; mean and standard error over dates (dates not independent: nourishment and storms act on all).

E_six_month_changes_2008_2010.note: Mead & Borrero (2011) p.4-5 (as recorded in 02_research/reefs/boscombe-surf-reef.md) report beach accretion of up to 60 m over >500 m within 6 months; the 0 m ODN contour at the CCO lines moved by the amounts listed (the claim may use another contour, line or reference; NOT reproduced here).

Rock mounds are in the tile; the beach and foreshore down to the water edge (about -2.3 mODN) are bare-earth. ONE DATE ONLY (10 y after Phase 1 was completed on 8 Mar 2012): no pre-construction beach survey exists in the repo.
borth-coastal-defence-reef.datum: metres MSL = mODN - 0.31 (MSL +0.31 mODN +-0.15 from a 4-level mean; Borth is macrotidal, MHWS +2.56, MLWS -1.74 mODN)

palm-beach-gold-coast.data_source: Garmin Navionics SonarChart iso-depth lines 1-10 m (1 m interval), read from z17 screenshots of maps.garmin.com (accessed 2026-10-05, "not for navigation"), converted to the canonical frame; model.js navionics.lines; METHODS_3D 3.5. prattes_two_surveys.data_source: Borrero & Nelsen (2003) Fig. 9, two bathymetric surveys (dashed = October 2000, four weeks after Phase I; solid = March 2001; METHODS_3D 3.10 / S10), contours -1..-4 m, vector paths digitised by 3d/bn_digitise.py into 3d/src/bn2003_fig9_contours.json (UTM 11N, datum not stated). Window 112 x 71 m, reef (58 x 29 m, 435 m2) not drawn; reef position inside the window is NOT known (+-150 m).
prattes_two_surveys.interpretation: Contour-to-contour shifts between the two surveys are listed; the window (about 2 x the reef length) has no control section and the reef is not drawn, so no lee/control test is possible. The paper itself states that the bathymetry did not change outside the contours made by the bags (S10).

albany_baseline.data_source: RHDHV Option B plan (2015, PRE-construction; reef built Mar-Jun 2025) contour crossings read on 8 shore-normal transects 20 m apart (x = -160..-20 m), distance from the beach-face line, 3d/src/levels2_raw.json (colour reading, +-10 m for the deeper lines; METHODS_3D 3.2). BMT 2018 soundings: spot values only.
albany_baseline.use: NATURAL alongshore variability of the -1..-3 m contours before the reef (trend + residual sd) = a noise floor for any future post-construction comparison; no post-construction bathymetry exists in the repo.

skipped.narrowneck-gold-coast: SKIPPED: the only measured bed is Corbett et al. (2023) Fig. 3 (ICM 2017 pre-works multibeam) digitised by colour hue into a 164 x 145 m window that is filled by the reef itself (no lee strip wider than 25 m, no control section; +-0.4 m colour-to-depth fit); outside the window the model bed is an ASSUMED alongshore-uniform profile (METHODS_3D 3.3: shoreward of y=190 assumed). City of Gold Coast DTM has NO underwater cells at the reef (07_scale/bathymetry/gold_coast, Q1). Gold Coast beaches are continuously nourished and sand-bypassed (insight b), so a shoreline signal would be confounded anyway. Literature pointers only (not tested here): Jackson et al. 2012 Fig. 16 (salient photo 20 May 2010), Mead & Borrero 2011 Fig. 5 (beach width envelope), Blacka et al. 2013 p.98 (called the widening an artefact of the reference line).
skipped.mount-maunganui-reef: SKIPPED: bed = ASSUMED alongshore-uniform profile (Navionics profile + a reef-centre offset; METHODS_3D 3.3) plus a digitised 2013 multibeam window (178 x 148 m, mostly the reef). The Navionics SonarChart z17 iso-lines (reef removed in 2014, so they show the ambient bed) trend by about 70 m over 320 m of coast near Mauao (2 m line: y = 320 m at x = -380 to 250 m at x = -60, 3d/navionics_isolines.json), i.e. the natural gradient is larger than any plausible reef signal; BoPRC p.29: the bed fluctuates by more than 1 m.
skipped.bunbury-airwave: SKIPPED: the Airwave bladder was in the water for about 3 days in Dec 2019 (installed 9-13 Dec, torn, removed within about 3 days; model.js lifecycle), so no sediment response is possible. The 2009 WA DoT airborne lidar grid in the model (10 m, gap-filled) is pre-structure.
skipped.prattes-reef-el-segundo: Seabed in the 3D model = ASSUMED alongshore-uniform profile (NOAA DEM 1/3 arc-sec + Navionics, METHODS_3D 3.4) -> SKIPPED for T1-T4; the two vector-contour surveys of Fig. 9 are summarised separately under "prattes_two_surveys".
skipped.southern-ocean-surf-reef-albany: SKIPPED: the reef was built in 2025 and the repo holds only the PRE-construction 2015 contours and an assumed alongshore-uniform profile (A4); a baseline of natural alongshore variability is given under "albany_baseline".
skipped.kovalam-reef-india / opunake-reef / burk: SKIPPED: no 3D model and no bathymetry grid or survey in the repo (their src/ folders hold imagery, outlines and PDFs only; opunake holds only a NZGD2000 grid-shift raster). Kovalam, Opunake and Burkitts: no data for a sediment test.
skipped.EMODnet DTM (07_scale/bathymetry/emodnet: NOT USABLE for this test: cells of 115 x 73 m (about the reef size), reef invisible in every release 2018-2024 (Boscombe cell max -4.87 mLAT vs model crest +0.56), one sounding per cell at Borth, interpolated at Haifa.

summary_table.magnitude: lee contours +15 m (0 m AHD), +17 (-1), +18 (-2), +27 (-3), +37 (-4) from the composite; +23..+43 m for -2..-6 m in the 2002 survey, versus controls 1.5-3.5 L away
summary_table.uncertainty: formal SE 2-8 m (placebo sd 1.5-4.6 m); the north-only and south-only controls give the same sign and agree within 10 m (anomaly_range in the JSON), so the offset is a robust spatial feature; its ATTRIBUTION is the problem, not its existence
summary_table.caveats: THE SAME BULGE IS IN THE 1995 PRE-CONSTRUCTION SURVEY: -5 m contour lee offset +20 m (1995) vs +25 m (2002) against adjacent strips; -6 m: +8 vs +10 m. The shoreward contours (0 to -3 m) have no pre-construction survey (1995 reaches only -2.45 m AHD, at n >= -167 m). Natural limestone reef lines of the Cottesloe coast are the likely cause (ASSUMPTION, not verified).

summary_table.test: T3 temporal change 1995 -> 2002 (before/after, lee vs adjacent controls)
summary_table.data: single-beam 1995-12 (pre) and 2002-02 (2.2 y after completion), TIN <= 25 m from a sounding
summary_table.magnitude: contour migration 2002-1995 in the lee relative to adjacent strips: +7.0 m (-4 m), +4.9 m (-5 m), +2.6 m (-6 m); bed change in the lee band (n = -165..-62 m): +0.03 m (lee +0.04 m, adjacent strips +0.03 / -0.04 m), volume +414 m3 over 96 % of the box
summary_table.uncertainty: noise floor: single-beam cell sd 0.29 m, pre-construction pair (1998 vs 1995) mean -0.10 m, sd 0.24 m; a +-0.1 m systematic survey offset = +-1,100 m3 over the lee box (11,300 m2)
summary_table.caveats: only 2.2 y after completion; controls are adjacent (1.4-2.7 half-lengths) and may lie inside the reef influence; the contour migration of +3..+7 m (formal SE 2-3 m) equals a bed rise of about 0.1-0.2 m at the local slope (1:15 to 1:40, ASSUMPTION read from the contour spacing) = within the +-0.1 m systematic offset between surveys; Ls/X = 0.52 (toe) / 0.44 (centre): the reef is short relative to its distance from the shore (thresholds not asserted here)

summary_table.test: T2 bed level in the lee band (n = -165..-62 m) vs controls
summary_table.signal: yes, but PRE-EXISTING (natural high in the lee)
summary_table.magnitude: lee band bed higher than the far controls by +0.60 m in 2002 (range +0.48..+0.72 over control choice) and by +0.75 m already in 1995 (single-sided control, n=9 samples), +0.39 m in the Perth_5m composite
summary_table.uncertainty: formal SE 0.05 m (2002); datum offsets between surveys +-0.1 m
summary_table.caveats: the high bed in the lee is as large before as after the reef: not a sediment-transport effect of the reef within the data

summary_table.test: T5 shoreline from beach-level surveys 2001-2012 (lee lines vs control lines)
summary_table.data: DoT WA beach point-elevation files Jan 2001 (13 months after completion), Feb 2002, Jan 2003, Aug 2011, Apr 2012; profile lines about 50 m apart; 2 lee lines, 6-8 control lines
summary_table.signal: yes (a lee shoreline bulge at every date) but shrinking, not growing; no pre-construction beach survey: inconclusive
summary_table.uncertainty: 3-4 lines per control strip, no formal SE; north-only and south-only controls differ by up to 19 m (anomaly_range); scatter between dates 10-26 m
summary_table.caveats: a salient that grows after construction would increase this number; it decreases by about 14 m in 11 y. A decaying initial feature, a natural feature (the offshore -5/-6 m contours show a lee hump already in 1995) and beach management at Leighton/Port Beach (NOT checked) are all compatible; the 2011-12 files cover a longer shore with a regional gradient of about 0.05 m/m

summary_table.data: post-construction soundings vs the 1998 pre-construction TIN; 1999-11 vs 2002-02 reef surface
summary_table.magnitude: ring 0-10 m outside the footprint +0.51 m (1999) / +0.42 m (2002) above the 1998 bed (rock spill, edge definition +-5 m); 10-25 m: -0.03 / +0.09 m; 25-50 m (2002) +0.13 m; 50-100 m +0.05 m. Reef surface 2002 minus 1999 at matched soundings +0.14 m (n=517, sd 0.37 m); 95th-percentile level inside the footprint -1.76 (1999) vs -1.83 m AHD (2002)
summary_table.uncertainty: sounding sd 0.3 m; positioning of soundings on a rough rock surface +-several m; SE in the JSON ignores spatial correlation
summary_table.caveats: an echo-sounder cannot separate sand cover from rock fall-down; negative values (toe scour) do not occur beyond 10 m

summary_table.test: BACI of the shoreline at 6 CCO lines (common-mode removed) and post-only alongshore pattern (11 lines)
summary_table.data: CCO beach profiles 2004-2026 (316 surveys on 11 lines); pre = 2004-07..2008-04 (5-16 dates), post = 2009-11..2026-03 (17-43 dates)
summary_table.signal: NO (at most a few metres; not distinguishable from management and tilt signals)
summary_table.magnitude: lee anomaly of the 0 m ODN contour +3.4 m (95% CI +1.3..+5.3), +1 m contour +1.9 m (-0.5..+4.3), volume above 0 m ODN +3.4 m3/m (-4.5..+10.5); post-only 11 lines: -0.2 +- 0.9 m (0 m), -1.2 +- 0.8 m (+1 m)
summary_table.uncertainty: bootstrap over survey dates; pre n = 5 dates only for 4 of the 6 lines; dates are not independent
summary_table.caveats: Poole Bay is groyned and recharged: the frontage-wide volume jumps (2006->2007: +72 m3/m; 2020->2021: +40 m3/m) are common to all lines (DERIVED indicator; recharge records not in the repo); about 23,000 m3 of sand was piled on the upper beach to build the reef (Rendle 2016 thesis p.125-127: 11,100 m3 stayed on the beach between the pier and the first groyne), which could mimic accretion; the shoreline tilts east-up/west-down by +3.0 m per 100 m after the reef (a tilt, not a local bulge); the largest 0 m contour advance 2009-11 -> 2010-04 was +3.0 m (the statement of up to 60 m in 6 months, Mead & Borrero 2011, is not reproduced at these lines)

summary_table.test: T1/T2 lee vs control contour position and bed level, single LiDAR date
summary_table.data: Welsh Government LiDAR DTM 2022-03-19 (1 m), beach and foreshore down to about -2.3 mODN; Phase 1 completed 2012-03-08
summary_table.magnitude: lee contour offset +30 m (0 m MSL), +40 (-1), +57 (-2) with a straight line through both controls; range over control choice +12..+48, +1..+77, +22..+93 m; bed level in the lee higher by +0.71, +0.78, +0.68 m (y = 40-100, 100-160, 160-220 m; ranges -0.11..+1.48, +0.26..+1.26, +0.24..+1.09)
summary_table.uncertainty: formal SE 2-9 m, but the choice of control (north strip vs south strip) changes the anomaly by 30-90 m: the beach has a strong natural north-south gradient (village frontage vs dune frontage)
summary_table.caveats: ONE survey 10 y after construction, no pre-construction beach survey in the repo; the south control strip shows the bulge is only +12 m (0 m MSL) and +0.5 m (-1 m) above the southern plateau, so a localised peak of about 20-26 m sits on top of a north-south step; the tile is only 730 m long so controls start 0.5 L from the reef; seasonal beach state (March) and bars not considered. Crest check from the project (HANDOFF): LiDAR minus design +0.14 +- 0.28 m, no burial.

summary_table.data: Garmin Navionics SonarChart 1-3 m iso-lines (z17 screenshots 2026-10-05), undated compilation; reef built 2019
summary_table.uncertainty: chart contours are smoothed (a 0.5 m label interval, positional error likely +-10 m, ASSUMPTION), datum and date unknown
summary_table.caveats: LOW CONFIDENCE; 4-6 m contours are bent by the reef shoal in the chart (+38 to +71 m) and are a chart artefact; the Gold Coast is nourished continuously (insight b), natural reef up-coast and bars are in the chart; no pre-reef contour set was digitised (Mortensen et al. 2015 Fig. 6a is read along ONE profile only).

summary_table.data: Borrero & Nelsen (2003) Fig. 9 vector contours -1..-4 m (112 x 71 m window)
summary_table.magnitude: all four contours moved offshore by +13 m on average (+9..+18 m per contour)
summary_table.uncertainty: survey datum / tide differences of 0.3 m would shift a 1:35 contour by about 10 m; digitising +-1 m
summary_table.caveats: no control section, reef not drawn, window about 2 reef lengths; the source states there is no change outside the bag contours
